nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\alpha)$ be the result of applying $f$ to $\alpha$ $|\alpha|$ times. Then $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ is a fixed point of $f$, that is, $f(\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)) = \mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$.
nodes.title: Finite iteration from the whole type reaches a fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ map subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$, and write $f^n$ for the $n$-fold iterate of $f$. Then $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ is the set $f^{|\alpha|}(\alpha)$, obtained by applying $f$ to the whole of $\alpha$ $|\alpha|$ times.
nodes.title: Greatest fixed point of a finset map by finite iteration

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\alpha)$ be the result of applying $f$ to $\alpha$ $|\alpha|$ times. If $Z \subseteq \alpha$ satisfies $Z \subseteq f(Z)$, then $Z \subseteq \mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.
